project.name: cc-history-viewer
project.description: A native Windows desktop app for browsing Claude Code conversation history. Built with Tauri + Express + React.

nodes.name: config.ts
nodes.summary: Server-wide configuration constants: resolves the Claude home directory (~/.claude) and the HTTP port from environment variables with sensible defaults.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Express application entry point that wires up CORS, JSON parsing, API routes, static client serving, and auto-opens the browser in standalone mode.

nodes.name: serveClient
nodes.summary: Scans for the client build directory and configures Express to serve static files with SPA fallback, falling back to API-only mode when no client dist is found.

nodes.name: findClientDist
nodes.summary: Probes multiple candidate paths (dev, bundled, Tauri embedded) to locate the built client distribution directory.

nodes.name: errorHandler.ts
nodes.summary: Express error-handling middleware that logs errors to stderr and returns a structured JSON error response.

nodes.name: errorHandler
nodes.summary: Catches unhandled Express errors, logs them via console.error, and responds with a JSON error object including message and optional details.

nodes.name: projects.ts
nodes.summary: API route handler for GET /api/projects — dynamically imports and calls scanProjects to list all Claude Code project directories.

nodes.name: search.ts
nodes.summary: API route handler for GET /api/search — dynamically imports and calls search to query across the Claude conversation history.

nodes.name: sessions.ts
nodes.summary: API route handler for GET /api/projects/:projectId/sessions — dynamically imports and calls getProjectSessions to list conversations for a project.

nodes.name: transcript.ts
nodes.summary: API route handler providing GET, PATCH, and DELETE endpoints for session transcripts — reads transcripts, updates metadata, and deletes sessions with their JSONL files.

nodes.name: historyReader.ts
nodes.summary: Reads the Claude conversation history JSONL file and provides search, filtering by session/project, and project-path encoding utilities.

nodes.name: readHistory
nodes.summary: Streams the history JSONL file line-by-line, parses each entry as JSON, and returns the full array of HistoryEntry objects.

nodes.name: search
nodes.summary: Performs a case-insensitive full-text search across history entries by display text, returning deduplicated SearchResult objects with match snippets.

nodes.name: pathEncoder.ts
nodes.summary: Encodes filesystem paths to filesystem-safe identifiers (replacing slashes/colons with dashes) and decodes them back with drive-letter extraction for Windows paths.

nodes.name: encodePath
nodes.summary: Encodes a real filesystem path to a safe identifier string by replacing backslashes and colons with dashes.

nodes.name: decodePath
nodes.summary: Decodes an encoded path identifier back to a real filesystem path, extracting Windows drive letters from a leading prefix.

nodes.name: getShortName
nodes.summary: Extracts a human-readable short project name from an encoded path by decoding and returning the deepest directory segment.

nodes.name: projectScanner.ts
nodes.summary: Core scanner that discovers Claude Code projects and sessions by reading the history file, resolving path mappings, and extracting session metadata from JSONL transcript files.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds an in-memory path-to-project map from the history JSONL, then scans session directories with streaming line-by-line JSONL parsing for metadata extraction.

nodes.name: buildPathMap
nodes.summary: Reads the history JSONL file and builds a Map from encoded project paths to display paths, resolving duplicates by keeping the most recent entry.

nodes.name: scanProjects
nodes.summary: Scans the Claude projects directory, finds JSONL session files per project, resolves display paths, and returns a sorted list of ProjectSummary objects.

nodes.name: getProjectSessions
nodes.summary: Lists all sessions for a given project by scanning the project's session directory, reading metadata for each JSONL file, and returning sorted SessionSummary objects.

nodes.name: readSessionMeta
nodes.summary: Streams a session JSONL file to extract display metadata: first user prompt, message count, timestamps, and conversation title from the first assistant message.

nodes.name: readCwdFromSession
nodes.summary: Reads the first entry of a session JSONL file to extract the cwd (working directory) field with early stream termination for efficiency.
nodes.languageNotes: Destroys the read stream after finding the first entry to avoid reading the entire file for a single field.

nodes.name: sessionDelete.ts
nodes.summary: Deletes a session by removing its JSONL transcript and metadata files, then rewriting the shared history file to exclude the deleted session's entries.

nodes.name: deleteSession
nodes.summary: Orchestrates full session deletion: removes the JSONL file, project session directory if empty, and filters the history file of entries referencing the deleted session.

nodes.name: filterHistoryFile
nodes.summary: Streams the shared history JSONL, rewrites it excluding all entries whose sessionId matches the deleted session, with atomic rename for safety.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses write-to-temp-then-rename pattern for atomic file replacement during history filtering.

nodes.name: sessionMetadata.ts
nodes.summary: Manages per-session metadata files (JSON) stored alongside transcripts — supports reading, writing, and partial updates for fields like customTitle and starred.

nodes.name: readMeta
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the session metadata JSON file, returning the metadata object or an empty default if the file does not exist.

nodes.name: writeMeta
nodes.summary: Writes a session metadata object to disk as JSON, creating the parent directory if needed.

nodes.name: updateMeta
nodes.summary: Merges a partial update into existing session metadata by reading, spreading the patch, and writing back the merged result.

nodes.name: transcriptReader.ts
nodes.summary: Reads and normalizes Claude Code transcript JSONL files — parses events, associates tool results, resolves sub-agents, and produces a structured TranscriptResponse.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a sophisticated event normalization pipeline handling multiple Claude message schemas (v1/v2), content blocks (thinking, text, tool_use, tool_result), and sub-agent transcript loading.

nodes.name: readTranscript
nodes.summary: Public entry point for reading a session transcript — parses the JSONL file, associates tool results with their calls, loads sub-agent transcripts, and returns the complete TranscriptResponse.

nodes.name: parseTranscriptFile
nodes.summary: Streams a single JSONL transcript file, parses each line as JSON, normalizes events, collects tool results in a Map, and returns events with pagination support.

nodes.name: normalizeEvent
nodes.summary: Transforms raw JSONL event objects into the uniform NormalizedEvent schema, handling multiple Claude API message shapes and extracting content blocks, tool calls, and token usage.

nodes.name: associateToolResults
nodes.summary: Post-processes normalized events to attach tool_result blocks to their corresponding tool_use blocks within each assistant message.

nodes.name: loadSubagents
nodes.summary: Discovers and loads sub-agent transcripts from the session directory, parsing each agent file and associating tool results within its events.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: TypeScript type definitions for the server domain model: HistoryEntry, ProjectSummary, SessionSummary, NormalizedEvent with ContentBlocks, TranscriptResponse, and SearchResult.

layers.name: API 层

layers.name: 服务层
layers.description: 服务端核心业务逻辑，包括 Claude Code 历史文件读取与搜索、项目扫描与会话发现、转录 JSONL 解析与事件规范化、会话元数据管理和会话删除，以及 Express 错误处理中间件

layers.name: 应用外壳与状态层
layers.description: React 应用启动引导和全局状态管理，通过 Context + useReducer 结合 localStorage 持久化实现设置、项目、会话、搜索结果和 Toast 通知的集中管理，包含根组件、DOM 挂载点和全局样式（含 6 套主题的 CSS 自定义属性）

layers.name: 类型层

layers.name: 工具层

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README provides a high-level map of the entire application: a Tauri v2 desktop shell that spawns a hidden Node.js Express server and opens a React frontend in a WebView2 window. It documents the three architectural layers, features (themes, search, markdown export), and the tech stack you will encounter throughout this tour.

tour.title: Express Server Entry Point
tour.description: The server entry point bootstraps the Express application by configuring CORS, JSON body parsing, mounting all API routes under /api, and serving the compiled React frontend as static files. In standalone mode, it also auto-opens the browser. This file is the nerve center that wires together every server-side concern.
tour.languageLesson: Express apps compose middleware and route handlers via app.use(). The order matters: CORS and body parsing must come before routes, and the error handler must be registered last to catch errors from all preceding middleware.

tour.title: Server Configuration and Error Handling
tour.description: Server-wide constants resolve the Claude home directory (~/.claude) and the HTTP port from environment variables with sensible defaults. The error-handling middleware sits at the end of the Express pipeline, logging errors to stderr and returning structured JSON responses. Together, these two modules provide the operational foundation every route handler depends on.
tour.languageLesson: Express error-handling middleware is identified by its four-parameter signature (err, req, res, next). It must be registered after all other middleware and routes, because Express calls error handlers only when next(err) is invoked or an error is thrown synchronously.

tour.title: Server Type Definitions
tour.description: The server's TypeScript types define the domain model vocabulary used throughout the backend: HistoryEntry, ProjectSummary, SessionSummary, NormalizedEvent with its ContentBlocks, TranscriptResponse, and SearchResult. These interfaces form the contract between the data-reading services and the API routes, ensuring type safety from file parsing through HTTP response.

tour.title: REST API Routes
tour.description: Four route modules expose the backend's capabilities over HTTP. The /api/projects, /api/projects/:projectId/sessions, and /api/search endpoints delegate to service-layer functions via dynamic imports. The /api/transcript route is the richest, supporting GET (read transcript), PATCH (update metadata like customTitle), and DELETE (remove a session and its JSONL file). Each route acts as a thin translation layer between HTTP and the business logic in the services.
tour.languageLesson: Express route handlers receive (req, res, next). Route parameters like :projectId are accessed via req.params. Dynamic imports (import() in the route body) can defer module loading until the endpoint is actually called, improving cold-start time for rarely-used endpoints.

tour.title: Core Business Services
tour.description: These services form the engine that reads and interprets Claude Code's data. historyReader parses the shared ~/.claude/history.jsonl file and provides search and filtering. projectScanner discovers projects and sessions by resolving file-system paths to project directories and reading per-session metadata. transcriptReader parses individual JSONL transcript files, normalizes events, associates tool results with their invocations, and resolves sub-agent sessions. pathEncoder handles the tricky problem of Windows drive-letter paths, encoding them as filesystem-safe identifiers.

tour.title: Session Metadata and Deletion
tour.description: Building on the project scanner from Step 6, sessionMetadata manages per-session JSON files stored alongside transcripts, supporting read, write, and partial updates for fields like customTitle and starred — enabling the rename and favorite features visible in the UI. sessionDelete removes a session by deleting its transcript and metadata files, then rewriting the shared history.jsonl to exclude the deleted session's entries, keeping the history file consistent.

tour.title: Client Entry Point and HTML Shell
tour.description: The React application boots from main.tsx, which renders the root App component into the DOM within React StrictMode and imports the global stylesheet. The index.html is the WebView2's entry point, pre-applying dark mode theme classes so there is no flash of unstyled content when the Tauri window opens. The App component wraps the Shell layout in AppProvider, establishing the global state context before any UI renders.
tour.languageLesson: React StrictMode is a development-only wrapper that double-invokes certain lifecycle methods to surface side-effect bugs. It does not affect production builds but helps catch impure renders during development.

tour.title: Global State Management and Client Types
tour.description: AppContext is the most depended-upon module in the entire codebase (fan-in of 25), serving as the central nervous system of the frontend. It uses React Context with useReducer for state management and persists settings, projects, sessions, search results, and toast notifications to localStorage. The client types mirror the server's domain model (Project, Session, NormalizedEvent, ContentBlock) and include the DEFAULT_FILTERS constant that controls which event types are visible by default.
tour.languageLesson: The combination of React Context + useReducer is a lightweight alternative to Redux or Zustand. The reducer function centralizes all state transitions as pure functions of (state, action) -> state, making the app's state changes predictable and debuggable. localStorage persistence on every state change ensures settings survive page refreshes.

tour.title: API Client Module
tour.description: The API client provides typed fetch helpers that all frontend components use to communicate with the Express backend from Step 2. It encapsulates endpoint methods for listing projects, fetching sessions, reading transcripts, updating metadata, deleting sessions, and performing full-text search. With a fan-in of 7, it is consumed by Shell, Sidebar, SearchBar, and ChatWindow — every component that needs server data.

tour.title: Application Shell and Layout
tour.description: The Shell component is the top-level layout controller (fan-out of 8), implementing keyboard shortcuts for session rename/delete and theme toggling, and orchestrating a two-panel layout with Sidebar and MainPanel. Sidebar manages project selection, session listing with inline rename and starring, and right-click context menus. MainPanel renders the ChatWindow for the currently selected session. Together, these three components define the spatial structure of the entire application window.

tour.title: Chat Rendering Core
tour.description: ChatWindow is the main chat view (fan-out of 9) that fetches transcript events from the API, applies visibility filters, provides markdown export, and supports session deletion. MessageBubble acts as a router, dispatching each event to AssistantMessage, SystemEvent, or UserMessage based on the event's role field. AssistantMessage (fan-out of 12) orchestrates the richest rendering path, composing TextBlock, ThinkingBlock, and ToolCallBlock for different content types within a single assistant turn.
tour.languageLesson: The MessageBubble component demonstrates the strategy pattern in React: a single component inspects an event's role and delegates to a specialized renderer. This keeps the rendering logic for each message type isolated while presenting a uniform interface to the parent ChatWindow.

tour.title: Specialized Chat Blocks and Filtering
tour.description: ThinkingBlock renders the AI's reasoning process in a collapsible section with a toggleable expand/collapse UI and signature preview. ToolCallBlock extracts a human-readable summary from tool inputs and shows raw JSON on expand. UserMessage and SystemEvent render user messages and system-level notifications respectively. FilterBar provides toggle buttons that control which event types (user/assistant/system/thinking/tool) are visible, plus a reader mode that hides all non-conversation content for distraction-free reading.

tour.title: Shared UI Primitives and Utilities
tour.description: Shared components provide reusable UI building blocks: CopyButton copies text to the clipboard with a visual confirmation, SettingsPanel offers a tabbed interface for theme, font, and size preferences (all persisted via AppContext), Toast renders auto-dismissing notifications, ContextMenu provides viewport-aware right-click menus, and InlineEdit enables in-place text editing. On the utility side, dateFormat provides relative time display (today/yesterday/N days ago) from ISO timestamps, and exportMarkdown converts conversation events into a downloadable Markdown file.

tour.title: Tauri Desktop Shell and Build Pipeline
tour.description: The final layer: the Rust-based Tauri v2 shell that wraps everything into a native Windows desktop app. main.rs suppresses the console window on release builds and delegates to lib.rs, which spawns the Node.js Express server as a child process, health-checks port 3001, and creates a WebView2 window pointing at the localhost frontend. The Tauri config orchestrates the full build: esbuild bundles the server into a single file, Vite builds the React client, and both are embedded as resources. The root package.json ties the monorepo together with concurrently for dev mode and a unified build command.
tour.languageLesson: Tauri v2 uses a Rust binary to create a lightweight native window (via the OS's webview) that hosts a web frontend. The tauri.conf.json controls the entire build pipeline via the 'beforeBuildCommand' and 'beforeDevCommand' fields, while the 'bundle.resources' field embeds the compiled server and client into the final executable. The Content Security Policy (CSP) in the config restricts which scripts and connections the webview allows, preventing XSS in the desktop context.
